a1.title: Power-On Test
a1.story: The board has just been soldered together. To test it, the engineer wants a known pattern in the registers. But the keypad is slow, so: as few loads as possible.
a1.task: End with A = $2A, X = $2B and Y = $2A. Use only one LDA, then copy and count to fill X and Y. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Copy A into X with TAX instead of loading X.
Copy A into Y with TAY instead of loading Y.
X has to be one more than A: use INX.

hints: Start with LDA #$2A.
TAX and TAY copy A into X and Y.
INX makes X one bigger. Then BRK.

a2.title: Today's Date
a2.story: The board has no clock. Every morning, the operator types today's date into memory, so other programs can read it.
a2.task: Store the day 10 at $0300, the month 11 at $0301 and the year 76 at $0302. Then copy the day from $0300 to the zero page address $40, by loading it from memory. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Copy the day by reading it from memory: LDA $0300.
Store the copy at $40.

hints: Each value: LDA #… then STA to its address.
10 is $0A, 11 is $0B and 76 is $4C, but decimal works too.
At the end: LDA $0300, then STA $40, then BRK.

a3.title: Shopping Total
a3.story: The board now runs the till of a tiny shop. Someone bought bread for 25, milk for 17 and an apple for 8.
a3.task: Add 25, 17 and 8 and store the total at $0300. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Clear the carry with CLC before adding.
Let the 6502 do the math: add the prices with ADC.

hints: Start with LDA #25.
CLC, then ADC #17 and ADC #8.
Store A with STA $0300, then BRK.

ac1-project.title: The Bank Account
ac1-project.story: A tiny bank keeps its only account at $0300 and counts every transaction at $0301. Today: the account is opened with 100, someone pays in 45 and takes out 30.
ac1-project.task: Store 100 at $0300. Add 45 to the balance and store it back, then subtract 30 and store it back. Count both transactions at $0301 with INC, so it ends at 2. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Pay in with ADC.
Pay out with SBC.
Set the carry with SEC before subtracting.
Count the transactions with INC $0301.

hints: Open the account: LDA #100, STA $0300.
Pay in: LDA $0300, CLC, ADC #45, STA $0300, INC $0301.
Pay out: LDA $0300, SEC, SBC #30, STA $0300, INC $0301. Then BRK.

a4.title: The Alarm
a4.story: A sensor writes its reading to $0300. A reading of 0 means the pipe is empty, and someone has to be warned.
a4.task: If $0300 is 0, store $FF at $0301 (alarm on). Otherwise store $01 at $0301 (all good). End with BRK.

requirements.message: Decide with BEQ or BNE.

hints: LDA $0300 sets the Z flag when the reading is 0.
BEQ ALARM jumps to a label when it's 0. Otherwise store $01 and BRK.
ALARM: LDA #$FF, STA $0301, BRK.

a5.title: The Multiplier
a5.story: Customers keep asking the board to multiply, but the 6502 has no multiply instruction. Time to build one.
a5.task: Multiply the number at $0300 by the number at $0301 and store the result at $0302. The result always fits in one byte. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Multiply by adding again and again with ADC.
Repeat the adding with a loop.

hints: LDA #0 for the total, LDX $0301 for the number of rounds.
Loop: CLC, ADC $0300, DEX, BNE back.
After the loop: STA $0302, then BRK.

a6.title: High Score
a6.story: Five players have finished the game. Their scores are at $0300 to $0304. The board has to find the winner's score.
a6.task: Find the biggest of the five bytes at $0300–$0304 and store it at $0310. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Walk through the scores with $0300,X.
Compare the scores with CMP.

hints: Start with the first score as the best: LDA $0300, then LDX #1.
Loop: CMP $0300,X. BCS skips ahead when A is already bigger or equal. Otherwise LDA $0300,X.
INX, CPX #5, BNE back to the loop. Then STA $0310.

ac2-project.title: The Grade Counter
ac2-project.story: A teacher typed the test scores of eight students into $0300–$0307. She wants two numbers from the board.
ac2-project.task: Count how many scores are 50 or more and store the count at $0310. Store the highest score at $0311. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Walk through the scores with $0300,X.
Compare each score with the pass mark, like CMP #50.

hints: Two loops are easiest: one counts the passes, one finds the highest score.
Counting: LDX #0, then LOOP: LDA $0300,X, CMP #50, BCC SKIP, INC $0310, SKIP: INX, CPX #8, BNE LOOP.
Highest: reuse the High Score quest, with CPX #8 and STA $0311.

a7.title: The Tripler
a7.story: Two numbers wait at $0300 and $0301. Both have to be tripled, and nobody wants to write the same code twice.
a7.task: Write a subroutine TRIPLE that takes a number in A and returns three times that number in A. Use it to store 3 × $0300 at $0310 and 3 × $0301 at $0311. End the main program with BRK.

requirements.message: Call your subroutine twice with JSR.
End the subroutine with RTS.

hints: Main program: LDA $0300, JSR TRIPLE, STA $0310, and the same for $0301 and $0311. Then BRK.
TRIPLE: STA $30 to keep the number, then add it twice.
TRIPLE: STA $30, CLC, ADC $30, CLC, ADC $30, RTS.

a8.title: Hello, KIM
a8.story: The board's first message to the world. The teletype is loaded with fresh paper and everyone is watching.
a8.task: Print HELLO, KIM-1! on the teletype. Keep the text in a .BYTE message with a 0 at the end, and print it with a loop. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Put the text into a .BYTE message, like MSG: .BYTE "HELLO, KIM-1!", 0.
Print the message with a loop, like LDA MSG,X.

hints: At the end: MSG: .BYTE "HELLO, KIM-1!", 0
LDX #0, then LOOP: LDA MSG,X and BEQ DONE.
JSR OUTCH, INX, JMP LOOP. DONE: BRK.

a9.title: The Scoreboard
a9.story: The arcade wants the score of the last game printed on the teletype, always with two digits.
a9.task: The score (0 to 99) is at $0300. Print SCORE: followed by the score with two digits, like SCORE: 42 or SCORE: 07. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Split the score into tens and ones by subtracting 10.

hints: Print the label first: a .BYTE message "SCORE: ", 0 and a loop, or one JSR OUTCH per letter.
Then the tens loop from the lesson: LDA $0300, LDX #0, TENS: CMP #10, BCC ONES, SEC, SBC #10, INX, JMP TENS.
ONES: PHA, TXA, CLC, ADC #'0, JSR OUTCH, PLA, CLC, ADC #'0, JSR OUTCH, BRK.

ac3-project.title: Times Table Printer
ac3-project.story: The school next door wants the board to print times tables. Each line has to be easy to read.
ac3-project.task: The number at $0300 (1 to 9) is the table. Print its multiples from 1 × to 10 ×, one per line, always with two digits. For 7: 07, 14, 21 … 70. Write a subroutine that prints a two-digit number. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Print each number with a subroutine that ends with RTS.
Start a new line with character 13.

hints: Keep the running multiple in $31 and the line counter in $32 (start at 10). X is busy in the print subroutine.
Loop: LDA $31, CLC, ADC $0300, STA $31, JSR PRINT2, LDA #13, JSR OUTCH, DEC $32, BNE LOOP.
PRINT2 is the tens-and-ones code from The Scoreboard, ending with RTS instead of BRK.

a10.title: Odd or Even
a10.story: The board is running a game of odds and evens. Every number at $0300 needs a verdict.
a10.task: If the number at $0300 is odd, store 1 at $0301. If it's even, store 0 at $0301. Use AND to test the lowest bit. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Test the lowest bit with AND #1.

hints: LDA $0300, then AND #1. A is now 1 for odd numbers and 0 for even ones.
That's already the answer! Just store it.
LDA $0300, AND #1, STA $0301, BRK.

a11.title: Times Ten
a11.story: The cash register counts in tens. It needs to multiply fast, without a slow adding loop.
a11.task: Multiply the number at $0300 (0 to 25) by 10 and store the result at $0301. Use shifts: 10 × N is 8 × N + 2 × N. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Multiply with ASL instead of adding in a loop.
Add 8 × N and 2 × N together with ADC.

hints: LDA $0300, ASL A gives 2 × N. Keep it: STA $30.
Two more ASL A give 8 × N.
CLC, ADC $30 adds the 2 × N. Then STA $0301 and BRK.

a12.title: The Big Multiply
a12.story: The tiny shop has grown: 200 boxes at 150 each. The total doesn't fit into one byte any more.
a12.task: Multiply $0300 by $0301 (both 0 to 255). Store the 16-bit result with the low byte at $0310 and the high byte at $0311. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Add with ADC to build the result.

hints: Simplest way: add $0300 to a 16-bit total, $0301 times. Clear $0310 and $0311 first.
Each round: CLC, LDA $0310, ADC $0300, STA $0310, LDA $0311, ADC #0, STA $0311.
Count the rounds with LDX $0301 … DEX, BNE. And skip the loop with BEQ when $0301 is 0!

ac4-project.title: The Hex Dump
ac4-project.story: Every machine-code programmer needs a hex dump: a printout of memory, byte by byte, in hex. Time to build your own.
ac4-project.task: Print the 8 bytes at $0300–$0307 in hex, with a space after each one, like 3C 0F A5 00 FF 12 80 7E. Get each byte's upper digit with LSR and its lower digit with AND #$0F. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Get the upper digit with LSR.
Get the lower digit with AND #$0F.

hints: A table HEX: .BYTE "0123456789ABCDEF" turns 0–15 into a character.
Upper digit: LDA $0300,X, LSR A four times, TAY, LDA HEX,Y, JSR OUTCH. Lower: LDA $0300,X, AND #$0F, TAY, LDA HEX,Y, JSR OUTCH.
Then LDA #' ', JSR OUTCH, INX, CPX #8, BNE back to the loop.

a13.title: Long Distance
a13.story: A truck driver logs three trips in the board's memory, each as a 16-bit number of kilometres. The boss wants the total.
a13.task: Three 16-bit numbers are stored low byte first at $0300/$0301, $0302/$0303 and $0304/$0305. Add them and store the total at $0310 (low) and $0311 (high). End with BRK.

requirements.message: Add the low and high bytes with ADC.

hints: First add trip 1 and trip 2, like in the lesson, and store the result at $0310/$0311.
Then add trip 3 to $0310/$0311: CLC, LDA $0310, ADC $0304, STA $0310, LDA $0311, ADC $0305, STA $0311.
Test 2: $00FF + $0001 needs the carry. Only one CLC per addition!

a14.title: The Copy Machine
a14.story: The board needs to back up a block of data before an experiment. How long the block is changes every day.
a14.task: The length of the block (1 to 32) is at $0300, and the block itself starts at $0301. Copy the block to $0380 using pointers and (zp),Y. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Copy through pointers, like LDA ($40),Y and STA ($42),Y.

hints: LDY #0, then LOOP: LDA ($40),Y, STA ($42),Y, INY.
Stop when Y reaches the length: CPY $0300, BNE LOOP. Test 3 checks that you don't copy one byte too many.

a15.title: Guess the Number
a15.story: The board thinks of a number from 0 to 9. The player types guesses until it's right. A classic of 1970s computer rooms.
a15.task: The secret number is at $0300. Read guesses with GETCH, one digit each. Print H if the guess is too high, L if it's too low, and when it's right print * and the number of guesses as one digit. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Read the guesses with JSR GETCH.

hints: Count the guesses in $31 (start at 0). GAME: JSR GETCH, SEC, SBC #'0, INC $31.
CMP $0300: BEQ WIN. BCS means the guess is bigger: print 'H. Otherwise print 'L. Then JMP GAME.
WIN: LDA #'*, JSR OUTCH, LDA $31, CLC, ADC #'0, JSR OUTCH, BRK.

ac5-project.title: The Nim Machine
ac5-project.story: Nim was one of the first games ever played against a computer. 16 sticks lie on the table. Players take turns taking 1, 2 or 3. Whoever takes the last stick wins. And the board never loses.
ac5-project.task: Start with 16 sticks. Each round: read the player's move with GETCH (a digit 1 to 3) and take that many. The board then takes 4 minus the player's move. Print the sticks left as two digits and a new line. When none are left, print I WIN. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Read the player's moves with JSR GETCH.
Take the sticks away with SBC.

hints: The board always takes 4 minus the player's move, so together they take exactly 4 each round. 16, 12, 8, 4, 0: the board takes the last stick.
But do the real math: sticks in $30. Read the key, SBC #'0, keep the move in $31. Then SEC, LDA $30, SBC $31, then SEC, SBC the board's move (4 - $31).
Print the sticks with your two-digit routine from The Scoreboard and LDA #13, JSR OUTCH. When $30 is 0, print I WIN from a .BYTE message.
